title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: GAR erotema 5 — first generative act; Cain/Seth tip
pass_a_gloss: Fifth erotema: if the first sin-act was an act of nature, why not the first generative act—so we are Cain or Seth in Adam? GAR brushes aside as paralogism tying Seth's birth to Adam's absolute first generative act (Gen. 4: that was at best third). Placeus flips the charge: the Learned Man missed the disjunction—Adam's generating is twofold: absolutely first, and first in the line from which we spring.
pass_b_english: GAR. Fifth it is asked. If the first act of sinning was an act of nature, why not also the first act of generating, so that in Adam we should be said to have been begotten as Cain, or as Seth? Reply. I pass over the learned man's paralogism, which ascribes Seth's begetting to the first act by which Adam generated, though that could only have been the third, Gen. 4. PLAC. What, I ask, is this paralogism? I fear it rather belongs to the Learned Man, who does not seem to have noticed the force of the disjunction I had used; namely there was a twofold act of Adam's generating: one absolutely first, the other first in the kind of those from whom we spring.
source_text: GAR. Quinto quaeritur. Si primus actus peccandi fuit actus naturae, cur non & primus actus generandi, ut in Adamo dicamur Cainum, aut Sethum genitos esse? Resp. Mitto viri docti paralogismum, Sethi genituram primo actui, quo Adamus generavit, attribuenti, qui tamen nonnisi tertius esse potuit, Gen. 4. PLAC. Quale, quaeso, est hoc paralogismum? Vereor ne id potius Viro docto tribui debeat, qui animadvertisse non videtur vim disjunctionis qua usus fueram; nempe duplex fuit actus generandi Adami, unus absolute primus, alter primus in genere eorum unde orti sumus.

choices.choice: GAR: Gen.4 third-act; Placeus: missed absolute vs line-first generating

bible_refs.note: Seth not Adam's absolute first generative act
